faq.title: Why are incoming and outgoing SMS messages blocked for 24 hours after transferring an eSIM?
faq.description: Under Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and TRAI consumer protection mandates, whenever a SIM card is swapped or converted to eSIM, telecom operators must enforce a mandatory 24-hour SMS blackout. This prevents cybercriminals who execute unauthorized SIM swaps from immediately receiving two-factor authentication banking OTPs.

faq.title: Can I simply scan the old eSIM QR code that I saved on my computer last year?
faq.description: No! eSIM QR codes and activation profiles are strictly single-use cryptographic tokens. Once a profile has been initialized and bound to a hardware modem's EID, that specific QR code is permanently invalidated. Transferring to a new phone requires generating a brand-new cryptographic profile linked to the new phone's unique EID.

faq.title: What is an EID and where do I find it on my new Android phone?
faq.description: An EID (Embedded Identity Document) is a globally unique 32-digit serial number assigned to the physical eUICC chip inside your smartphone. You can find it by navigating to Settings > About phone > Status information > EID, or by opening your phone dialer and keying in the USSD code: *#06#.

html:
The Transition to Physical-SIM-Free Hardware

The era of fiddling with flimsy plastic nano-SIM cards and hunting for paperclips to pop open SIM trays is rapidly coming to an end. Flagship and mid-range Android smartphones—including the Samsung Galaxy S-series, Google Pixel devices, Motorola Edge models, and modern OnePlus flagships—are increasingly adopting eSIM (embedded SIM) technology. An eSIM replaces the removable plastic card with a permanently soldered, reprogrammable microchip inside the smartphone's chassis, known as an eUICC (Embedded Universal Integrated Circuit Card).

While an eSIM offers superior security (a thief cannot physically eject your SIM to bypass lock-screen authentication), transferring an active eSIM profile from an old Android smartphone to a new Android device during an upgrade frequently causes extreme confusion. Unlike iPhones which utilize Apple's proprietary Bluetooth Quick Transfer protocol, Android devices in India rely on carrier-specific remote SIM provisioning architecture (RSP). If you execute the steps in the wrong sequence or delete your old eSIM prematurely, you risk total cellular disconnection. This exhaustive step-by-step guide explains how to transfer your eSIM profile across Reliance Jio, Bharti Airtel, and Vodafone Idea (Vi) safely without visiting a physical telecom store.

The 3 Golden Rules Before Initiating an eSIM Transfer

Before typing a single SMS or touching settings, commit these three non-negotiable security rules to memory:

  1. NEVER Delete the Old eSIM Profile Prematurely: Do not navigate to your old phone's settings and tap 'Remove eSIM' or 'Erase eSIM'. Your old phone must remain powered on, with the old eSIM active, to receive mandatory confirmation SMS messages, verification phone calls, and one-time passwords (OTPs) from your telecom carrier.
  2. Connect Both Devices to Stable Wi-Fi: Downloading and provisioning a new eSIM cryptographic profile requires communicating with the carrier's Remote SIM Provisioning server (SM-DP+). Ensure both smartphones are connected to high-speed home Wi-Fi throughout the procedure.
  3. Prepare for the Mandatory 24-Hour SMS Blackout: Under Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and TRAI regulations, all incoming and outgoing SMS services are suspended for exactly 24 hours following any SIM change or eSIM transfer. This is a deliberate anti-fraud measure designed to prevent cybercriminals from stealing your bank OTPs via SIM swapping. Do not plan urgent banking transactions or UPI resets during this 24-hour window.

Step 1: Locate the 32-Digit EID Number on Your NEW Phone

Every eSIM-capable smartphone possesses a unique 32-digit hardware serial number known as the EID (Embedded Identity Document). You need this number to tell your telecom carrier which physical microchip to provision:

  1. Take your NEW Android smartphone.
  2. Open the Phone dialer app and dial: *#06#.
  3. A system modal will appear showing your IMEI 1, IMEI 2, and a 32-digit number labeled EID accompanied by a barcode.
  4. Alternative Path: Go to Settings > About phone > Status information > EID.
  5. Press and hold to copy the 32-digit EID number, or write it down with absolute precision. A single mistyped digit will cause the carrier's provisioning engine to fail.

Carrier-Specific Transfer Procedures

1. How to Transfer a Jio eSIM Between Android Phones

Reliance Jio utilizes an automated two-way SMS and interactive voice response (IVR) verification process:

  1. On your OLD phone (where your Jio eSIM is currently active), open the Messages app.
  2. Send an SMS to 199 with the text:
    GETESIM <32-digit EID of New Phone> <15-digit IMEI of New Phone>
    (Example: GETESIM 89049032005008882600035841209876 358941209876543).
  3. Within 2 minutes, Jio will reply with a confirmation SMS containing a 19-digit virtual eSIM number.
  4. Send a secondary confirmation SMS to 199:
    SIMCHG <19-digit virtual eSIM number>.
  5. After 2 hours, you will receive an automated call from Jio on your old phone. Answer the call and press 1 on your dial pad to provide explicit consent for the SIM change.
  6. Once consent is logged, you will receive an SMS confirmation stating: 'Your eSIM profile is ready for download'.
  7. On your NEW phone: Go to Settings > Connections (or Network & internet) > SIM manager > Add eSIM.
  8. Select Scan QR code (Jio will email the profile to your registered email address), or simply wait: on Samsung and Pixel devices, an automated system notification will appear: 'Jio eSIM ready to install'. Tap the notification and confirm installation.
  9. Once the new eSIM displays signal bars on the new phone, you may safely delete the inactive profile from the old device.

2. How to Transfer an Airtel eSIM (Via Airtel Thanks App)

Bharti Airtel provides the most seamless in-app digital transfer workflow in India:

  1. Connect your NEW phone to Wi-Fi. Install and open the Airtel Thanks app.
  2. Sign in using your Airtel mobile number (the OTP will arrive on your old phone).
  3. In the Airtel Thanks search bar, type 'eSIM' and select Upgrade to eSIM / Transfer eSIM.
  4. Select the option: 'Transfer to another device'.
  5. Enter the 32-digit EID number of your NEW phone when prompted. Tap Continue.
  6. Verify the transaction with the 6-digit OTP sent to your old phone.
  7. Airtel will initiate automated voice verification: you will receive an IVR call within 10 minutes. Press the designated confirmation key to approve the transfer.
  8. On your NEW phone, navigate to Settings > Mobile network > Add eSIM. Scan the QR code sent to your registered email address. The profile will download and register on Airtel 5G Plus within 2 hours.

3. How to Transfer a Vodafone Idea (Vi) eSIM

  1. On your OLD phone, send an SMS to 199:
    eSIM <your registered email address>.
  2. If your email is verified, Vi sends an immediate confirmation SMS. Reply to 199 with: ESIMY within 15 minutes.
  3. You will receive an automated consent call from Vi. Press 1 to approve.
  4. Vi will transmit an official activation QR code directly to your registered email address.
  5. On your NEW phone, open Settings > SIM manager > Add eSIM > Scan QR code. Point your camera at the QR code on your computer screen. The profile downloads in under 60 seconds.

What to Do If Your Old Phone Is Broken or Water-Damaged

If your old phone was crushed, dropped in water, or stolen, you cannot receive the mandatory verification SMS or IVR phone calls required for digital self-service transfer. In this scenario, digital transfer is legally impossible under telecom security guidelines.

The Emergency Recovery Protocol:

  • Visit your nearest official carrier gallery (Jio Store, Airtel Store, or Vi Store) in person.
  • Carry your original physical Aadhaar Card or Voter ID.
  • Inform the customer service executive that your previous handset is non-functional and request an In-Person Physical-to-eSIM Swap.
  • The executive will execute biometric fingerprint verification on their authorized terminal and directly provision your new phone's 32-digit EID on the spot.

Under the Hood: The GSMA SGP.22 Architecture Behind eSIM

To troubleshoot eSIM transfers, it is helpful to appreciate the cryptographic architecture governing remote SIM provisioning. Consumer eSIM follows the GSMA SGP.22 standard. The architecture consists of three interconnected systems:

  • eUICC (Embedded Universal Integrated Circuit Card): The secure, tamper-proof hardware element soldered onto your smartphone's circuit board, possessing a permanent cryptographic certificate authority (PKI) key issued by GSMA.
  • SM-DP+ (Subscription Manager Data Preparation+): The carrier's cloud server responsible for creating, encrypting, and storing your personalized operator profile (containing your phone number, IMSI, and authentication keys Ki).
  • LPA (Local Profile Assistant): The software client embedded inside your Android OS that communicates with the SM-DP+ server to download, decrypt, and install the profile onto the eUICC chip.

When you scan a carrier QR code or submit your 32-digit EID, the SM-DP+ server packages your mobile plan into an encrypted payload that can only be decrypted by your new phone's physical hardware eUICC chip. This mathematical binding explains why an eSIM profile cannot be cloned or transferred across devices without the carrier generating a brand-new cryptographic envelope.

Dual eSIM Management: How Modern Android Manages Multiple Profiles

Modern Android smartphones—most notably Google Pixel 7/8/9, Samsung Galaxy S24/S25 series, and newer OnePlus flagships—incorporate Multiple Enabled Profiles (MEP) technology. Prior to MEP, an eSIM chip could only keep one single carrier profile active at any moment; if you wanted dual-SIM functionality, you were forced to use one physical nano-SIM and one eSIM.

With MEP support, the eUICC chip splits its baseband radio channels, enabling you to store up to 8 or 10 distinct eSIM profiles in memory while keeping two eSIM profiles simultaneously active (Dual Active Dual Standby) without inserting any physical SIM card whatsoever. During the transfer process to a new device, you can migrate both your primary personal number and secondary business number onto the single eUICC chip, toggling data and voice channels dynamically in Android's SIM Manager interface.

Preventative Architecture & Companion Recommendations

Once your new eSIM is activated on your upgraded smartphone, ensure you safeguard your identity and connection.
